description: TLS handshake analysis: version distribution, cipher suites, JA3/JA3S fingerprints, SNI, certificate issuers, latency, resumption method, and raw handshake detail.

panels.title: Total Handshakes
panels.description:
Total TLS handshake events captured.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Unique TLS Versions
panels.description:
Cardinality of tls.version. Ideally only TLS 1.2 and 1.3; older versions are insecure.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Session Resumption %
panels.description:
Percentage of TLS sessions using resumption (tls.resumed=true). Higher is better for performance.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Unique Servers
panels.description:
Cardinality of destination.ip for TLS traffic.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Unique SNI
panels.description:
Cardinality of TLS Server Name Indication values. Shows how many distinct services are accessed via TLS.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Avg Handshake Latency
panels.description:
Average TLS handshake duration (event.duration). High latency may indicate MITM or overloaded endpoints.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Handshakes Over Time
panels.description:
TLS handshake rate per interval. Correlates with new secure connections.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: TLS Version Distribution
panels.description:
Handshakes split by TLS version. TLS 1.0/1.1 should be zero; 1.3 preferred.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: JA3 Client Fingerprints
panels.description:
Top JA3 hashes identifying client TLS implementations. Known-bad JA3 hashes indicate malware C2 (MITRE ATT&CK T1071).
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: JA3S Server Fingerprints
panels.description:
Top JA3S hashes identifying server TLS implementations. Unusual JA3S for known services may indicate interception.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Server Name (SNI)
panels.description:
Top TLS Server Name Indication values. Shows which services are accessed via TLS without decryption.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Destination Domain
panels.description:
Top destination domains for TLS connections. Complements SNI with reverse DNS information.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Cipher Suites
panels.description:
Top cipher suites used. Modern AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM, CHACHA20) are preferred.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Certificate Issuers
panels.description:
Top certificate issuers. Helps identify CA distribution and internal vs external certs.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Handshake Latency
panels.description:
TLS handshake latency over time. Spikes indicate network issues or computational overhead from key exchange.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Resumption Method
panels.description:
TLS session resumption method (session ID vs session ticket). Indicates server-side session cache behavior.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: Traffic Direction
panels.description:
TLS traffic direction. All TLS from our hosts is expected to be egress (outbound connections).
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls

panels.title: TLS Detail
panels.description:
Raw TLS handshake details: SNI, domain, version, cipher, JA3/JA3S fingerprints, resumption, direction, latency.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.tls
